translations.text: The word of the Lord that came to Joel son of Pethuel.
Hear this, elders, and listen, all you who live in the land. Has anything like this happened in your days or in the days of your fathers?
Tell your children about it, and let your children tell their children, and their children another generation.
What the caterpillar left, the locust ate; what the locust left, the young locust ate; and what the young locust left, the grasshopper ate.
Sober up, you who drink wine! Weep and wail, all you who drink wine to become drunk, because joy and gladness have been taken away from your mouths.
For nations have come up into the land, [?], powerful and beyond counting. Their teeth are lions' teeth, and their fangs are those of a young lion.
They laid waste my vine and broke my fig tree. They stripped it, searched it out, and abandoned it, leaving its branches white.
Weep for me over the bride who has put on sackcloth for the husband of her youth.
The [?] and the drink offering have been removed from the house of the Lord. Wail, priests who offer sacrifices.
For the fields are ruined, and the land mourns, because the grain is ruined, the wine has dried up, and the oil has disappeared.
Be ashamed, farmers, and weep, keepers of vineyards, over the wheat and barley, because the harvest has perished from the fields.
The vine has dried up, and the fig tree has perished. The pomegranate, the palm, the apple tree, and all the trees of the countryside have dried up, and the joy of humankind has been put to shame.

Lament and put on sackcloth, priests; weep, you who offer sacrifices. Go and lie down in sackcloth, you who offer sacrifices to the Lord, because offerings and drink offerings have ceased from the house of the Lord.
Consecrate a fast and proclaim a time of supplication. Gather the elders and everyone who lives in the land into the house of our God, and cry out together to the Lord.
Alas for me! Alas for me on that day! For the day of the Lord has drawn near, and it will come like this, with scourge upon scourge.
Before your eyes, food disappears, and joy and gladness disappear from the house of your God.
The calves have perished in their stalls, the storehouses are ruined, and the granaries have been torn down, because the grain has dried up.
What, then, shall we do for ourselves? The herds of cattle have wept because their pasture is gone, and the grazing grounds of the sheep have disappeared.
To you, Lord, I cry out, because fire has consumed the beauty of the wilderness, and flames have burned the trees of the forests.
Even the animals of the field have looked up to you, because the springs of water have dried up and fire has consumed the beauty of the wilderness.
Blow the horn in Zion and proclaim on my holy mountain. Let everyone who lives in the land tremble, because the day of the Lord has arrived and is near.

A day of darkness and storm, a day of cloud and gloom. Like dawn, a great and powerful people spreads over the mountains. Nothing like it has existed since the creation of the world, and nothing like it will happen again afterward, through the years of generation after generation.
[?] Fire devours before it, and flames burn behind it. Before it, the land is like a garden of delight; behind it, the land becomes like a scorching desert, and nothing escapes it.
Their appearance is like that of horses, and they run like horses.
With a sound like chariots, they leap over the mountaintops, and with a sound like flames consuming stubble, like a great and powerful army fighting in a charge.
The nations tremble before it, and the faces become—and the faces of them all become—like the blackening of a cooking pot.
They run like warriors and climb the walls like courageous men. They all proceed along their own paths and do not stray from them.
They do not separate from one another. Carrying their field implements, they run and perish in their [?].
They gather in cities and run along the walls. They climb into houses and enter through the windows like thieves.
The earth will tremble before them, and the heavens will shake. The sun and the moon will grow dark, and the stars will lose their light.

The Lord will raise his voice before his army, for his camp is exceedingly large, and the fulfillment of his word is mighty. For the day of the Lord is great and terrifying, and it will appear with great power. What is its extent? Who can endure it?
Even now, says the Lord God, return to me with all your hearts, with fasting, mourning, and weeping.
Tear your hearts, not your clothes, and return to the Lord your God, for he is merciful and compassionate, slow to anger and abundant in mercy, and he relents concerning disaster.
Who knows whether he will turn back and relent, and leave a blessing behind him, a sacrifice and a drink offering for the Lord our God?
Blow the horn in Zion, consecrate a fast, and proclaim a time of supplication.
Bring in the people and consecrate your assembly. Choose the leaders and gather the infants who nurse at the breast. Let the bridegroom come out of his chamber and the bride from her canopy.

Let the priests who offer sacrifices to the Lord weep between the horns of the altar, and let them say, “Spare your people, Lord, and do not disgrace your inheritance, so that the nations do not triumph over them and the nations do not say, ‘Where is their God?’”
The Lord became jealous for his land and had compassion on his people.
The Lord answered them and said to his people, “Look, I am sending you grain, wine, and oil, and you will be satisfied. I will not make you an object of contempt among the nations.”

I will drive away from you those from the south, and drive them into a desert land. I will destroy them completely in the eastern sea. Their stench will rise, and their [?] will rise, because they have done great deeds.
Take courage, land, and rejoice and be glad, for the Lord has done great things.
Take courage, animals of the wilderness, for the pastures of the desert are rich, the trees have borne fruit, and the vine and the fig tree have yielded their abundance.
Rejoice and be glad in the Lord your God, children of Zion, for he has given you food in righteousness, and he will send you the spring and autumn rains as before.
The threshing floor will be filled with grain, and the vats will overflow with wine and oil.
I will compensate you for the years consumed by the locusts, worms, [?], and caterpillars—my army that I sent against you.
Be nourished, eat, and be satisfied, and praise the name of the Lord our God, for he has done wonders for you. My people will never again be put to shame.
You will know [?] that I am among Israel, and that I am the Lord your God, and there is no other besides me. My people will never again be put to shame.
After this I will pour out my Spirit upon you, all humankind. Your sons and daughters will prophesy, your elders will dream dreams, and your young men will see visions.
At that time I will pour out my Spirit even upon my male servants and my female servants.
I will perform wonders in heaven above and on earth below: blood, fire, and clouds of smoke.
The sun will grow dark, and the moon will become blood, before the great day of the Lord arrives and is revealed.
Everyone who calls on the Lord [?] will be saved. For on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem they will be saved, as the Lord has said, and [?] those whom the Lord has called.
For at that time, in those days, I will bring back the captives of Judah and Jerusalem.

I will gather all the nations and bring them down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. There I will bring charges against them concerning my people and my inheritance, Israel, who were scattered among the nations, and concerning my land, which they divided among themselves.
They cast lots for my people, gave their sons to prostitutes, and sold their daughters for wine, which they drank.

What have I to do with you, Tyre and Sidon and all Galilee of the Philistines? Are you taking revenge on me? Are you holding a grudge against me? Quickly and swiftly I will repay you upon your own heads.
Look, you have taken my gold and my silver, and you have brought my tithes and beautiful things into your houses.
You sold the children of Judah and the children of Jerusalem to the children of the pagans, to remove them from their own land.
Look, I will raise them up from the land where you sold them, and I will bring your punishment back upon your own heads.
I will take vengeance on your sons and daughters through the people of Judah, and I will take vengeance on you where you were taken captive among distant, far-off nations, for the Lord has spoken.
Proclaim this among the nations: prepare for war and rouse the warriors. Bring them out, and let all the fighting men go up.
Turn your plows into swords and your sickles into spears. Let the weak person say, “I am strong.”
Let all the nations gather and go; let them [?] the warriors.
Let all the nations rise and go up to the valley of Jehoshaphat, for there I will sit and judge all the nations and [?] lands.
Send out the sickle, for the harvest is ripe. Come in and tread, for the winepress is full and the wine overflows from the presses. Look, their wickedness has become great.
Cry out in the valley of judgment and raise your voices, for the day of the Lord has drawn near in the valley of judgment.
The sun and moon will grow dark, and the light of the stars will fade.
The Lord will roar from Zion and raise his voice from Jerusalem, and heaven and earth will shake. The Lord will spare his people, and the Lord will strengthen the people of Israel.
Then you will know that I am the Lord your God, who dwells in Zion, on my holy mountain. Jerusalem will become a holy city, and no one from another nation will pass through it anymore.
On that day honey will drip from the mountains, milk will flow from the hills, and water will spring up along all the roads of Judah. A spring will gush forth, and the river of Shittim will flow out.
The land of Egypt will become desolate, and Edom will become a wilderness. They will perish because of their sins against the people of Judah, for they shed innocent blood in their land.
But Judah will remain forever, and Jerusalem from generation to generation.
I will avenge their blood and will not acquit, for the Lord dwells in Zion.
